simplifyingQuestion.whyItMatters: A cheap input-owned state update that preserves its future consequences would simplify contextual initialization and later transition design. The same future-sufficiency demand applies to denoising and pixel readout. A local descent-preserving compiler is only one concrete step toward that, not the complete answer.
simplifyingQuestion.loosen: Do not require exact native hidden-coordinate parity, every-row gains, or a global quotient proof before exploratory construction. Change state representation and algorithm when measured own continuation supports it.
simplifyingQuestion.tighten: Require explicit input ownership, source/finite policy, paid computation, parent representability when a zero-update claim is made, and alignment between the proposed update and the actual admitted writer. Do not infer a BF16 zero-dose state from two secants.
simplifyingQuestion.doNotSubstitute: No whole-history leaves, native gains/radii, supplied contextual states, dense learned maps renamed as symbols, or hand-authored scene renderer may fill the unresolved boundaries.
